outcome.technical: plugins/audit/scripts/git/_worktrees.py: new _held_moved_on(fn, tree, held, commits) returns the sorted held paths whose bytes match neither the copy (_holds) nor any of the commits (_reads_as, absent where the commit has none). restore_copy now refuses before _undo when any path is either the existing unheld newer work (_newer_work, minus held) or one of these held paths. It reuses the existing refusal: restored False, the paths named, the copy kept, nothing written. The heads tuple is computed once and passed to both. restore_copy's docstring now states the full contract: never write over newer work, held or not. The old wording ('the paths it holds are what a restore is asked to write over') is gone. tests/test__worktrees.py: un9 edits held a.txt after a kill-in-undo to bytes that are none of copy/base/head and expects a refusal naming a.txt, with the copy kept, bytes, status and HEAD unchanged. un10 is the over-fire twin: a.txt already holds the copy's bytes, and the restore must still run and restage n.txt. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: the _worktrees section's restore sentence (around line 1115) now names the held-path refusal (un9) and the copy-bytes allowance (un10).
